14.subject: Botany
14.text: In a plant organ which is covered by periderm and in which the stomata are absent, some gaseous exchange still takes place through
14.sol:
Due to continued formation of secondary tissues in the older stem and roots however the epidermis gets stressed and ultimately tends to rupture and followed by death of epidermal cells and outer tissues, and a new protective layer is developed called periderm. Structurally it consists of three parts Phellogen or Cork cambium, phellem or cork and phelloderm.
Usually in the periderm of most plants, certain areas with loosely arranged cells have been found, which possess more or less raised and corky spots where the underneath tissues break through the epidermis. Such areas are universally found in the stems of woody plants. These broken areas are called lenticels, which perform the function of exchange of gases in the absence of stomata.

According to Henry's law :-

$\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{xK}_{\mathrm{H}}$ For $\mathrm{N}_2$ :- $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{N}_2}=\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{N}_2} \mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{H}}  \left(\mathrm{N}_2\right)$ For $\mathrm{O}_2$ :-  $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{O}_2}=\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{O}_2} \mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{H}$}  $\left(\mathrm{O}_{2}\right)$
We have, $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{N}_2}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{O}_2}$, $\mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{H}$}$\left(\mathrm{N}_{2}\right)=76$.48 $\mathrm{k} bar,  \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}}\left(\mathrm{O}_{2}\right)=3486 \mathrm{k} bar
 \begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow $\frac{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{N}_2}}{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{O}_2}}=\frac{\left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{N}_2}}{\mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{H}}\left(\mathrm{N}_2\right)}\right)}{\left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{O}_2}}{\mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{H}}\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)}\right)}=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{P}}{\mathrm{N}_2}}{\mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{H}}\left(\mathrm{N}_2\right)} \times \frac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}}\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)}{\frac{\mathrm{P}}{\mathrm{O}_2}}$\\ & $=\frac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}}\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}}\left(\mathrm{N}_2\right)}=\frac{34.86}{76.48}=0.45\end{aligned}$

6941.text: The radius of a circle whose center is $(2,1)$ and one of the chords is a diameter of the circle $x^2+y^2-2 x-6 y+6=0$, is units.

(i)$ and (ii), we obtain end points of diameter be(1,1) and (1,5)$. Now, we have to find radius of circle having centre at $(2,1)$ and one of its chord having end point $(1,1) and (1,5)$ \\ From given circle, $\begin{aligned}$x²+y² & =r² \\ x=$\sqrt{(2-1)^2+(1-3)^2}$& =$\sqrt{5}$\\ y=$\sqrt{(1-1)^2+(3-1)^2}$& =$\sqrt{4}$\\ \Rightarrow \quad r²=x²+y²=5+4 & =9 \\ \Rightarrow \quad r & =3 \end{aligned} $

8490.text: $x=\cos \theta, y=\sin 5 \theta \Rightarrow\left(1-x^2\right) \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}-x \frac{d y}{d x}$ is equal to
8490.sol:
Given, $x=\cos \theta, y=\sin 5 \theta\frac{d x}{d \theta}=-\sin \theta, \frac{d y}{d \theta}=5 \cos 5 \theta\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d y / d \theta}{d x / d \theta}=-\frac{5 \cos 5 \theta}{\sin \theta} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)=\frac{d}{d \theta}\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right) \cdot \frac{d \theta}{d x} \\ & =\frac{d}{d \theta}\left(\frac{-5 \cos 5 \theta}{\sin \theta}\right) \cdot \frac{1}{-\sin \theta} \\ & =\left(\frac{\sin \theta \sin 5 \theta \cdot 25+5 \cos 5 \theta \cos \theta}{\sin ^2 \theta}\right) \cdot \frac{1}{-\sin \theta} \\ & =-\frac{25 \sin 5 \theta}{\sin ^2 \theta}-\frac{5 \cos 5 \theta \cos \theta}{\sin ^3 \theta}\end{aligned}$
Now,
$\begin{aligned} &\left(1-x^2\right) \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}-x \frac{d y}{d x} \\ &=\left(1-\cos ^2 \theta\right)\left(\frac{-25 \sin 5 \theta}{\sin ^2 \theta}-\frac{5 \cos 5 \theta \cos \theta}{\sin ^3 \theta}\right) \\ &-\cos \theta\left(\frac{-5 \cos 5 \theta}{\sin \theta}\right) \\ &= \sin ^2 \theta\left(\frac{-25 \sin 5 \theta}{\sin ^2 \theta}-\frac{5 \cos \theta \cos 5 \theta}{\sin ^3 \theta}\right) \\ &+\frac{5 \cos \theta \cos 5 \theta}{\sin \theta} \\ &=-25 \sin 5 \theta-\frac{5 \cos \theta \cos 5 \theta}{\sin \theta}+\frac{5 \cos \theta \cos 5 \theta}{\sin \theta} \\ &=-25 \sin 5 \theta \\ &=-25 y\end{aligned}$

Let roots are $\frac{a}{r}, a, a r$

12758.text: If $\frac{1}{6} \sin \theta, \cos \theta$ and $\tan \theta$ are in geometric progression, then the solution set of $\theta$ is
12758.sol:
Given that, terms $\frac{1}{6} \sin \theta, \cos \theta$ and $\tan \theta$ are in GP.
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad \cos ^2 \theta=\frac{1}{6} \sin \theta \times \tan \theta \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \cos ^2 \theta=\frac{\sin ^2 \theta}{6 \cos \theta} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 6 \cos ^3 \theta-\sin ^2 \theta=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 6 \cos ^3 \theta-1+\cos ^2 \theta=0
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad 6 \cos ^3 \theta+1+\cos ^2 \theta=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 6 \cos ^3 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta-1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 6 \cos ^3 \theta+4 \cos ^2 \theta-3 \cos ^2 \theta+2 \cos \theta-2 \cos \theta-1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 6 \cos ^3 \theta-3 \cos ^2 \theta+4 \cos ^2 \theta-2 \cos \theta+2 \cos \theta-1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 3 \cos ^2 \theta(2 \cos \theta-1)+2 \cos \theta(2 \cos \theta-1)+1(2 \cos \theta-1) \\
& \quad=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad(2 \cos \theta-1)\left(3 \cos ^2 \theta+2 \cos \theta+1\right)=0
\end{aligned}$
For $3 \cos ^2 \theta+2 \cos \theta+1=0$ value of $\cos \theta$ will be imaginary so only $2 \cos \theta-1=0$ will be considered to find $\cos \theta$.
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 \cos \theta-1=0 \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\cos \frac{\pi}{3} \\
& \therefore \quad \theta=2 \mathrm{n} \pi \pm \frac{\pi}{3}
\end{aligned}$

17461.subject: Chemistry
17461.text: Identify, from the following, the diamagnetic, tetrahedral complex
17461.sol: (a) Ni in $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{Cl})_4\right]^{2-}$ exist as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ion. Cl is a weak field ligand (high spin). It will not cause pairing of electrons. Hence, configuration of $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{Cl})_4\right]^{2-}$ is Tetrahedral with two unpaired electrons (i.e., paramagnetic) and has $s p^3$ hybridisation. (b) In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)_3\right]^{3-},\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)_3^{2-}$ is a bidentate ligand thus, give octahedral structure. (c) In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}$, Ni exist as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ion. $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand (low spin). Causes pairing of electrons of $3 d$ orbital. Hence, the structure of is square planar and it is diamagnetic. (d) In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4\right]$, Ni has zero oxidation state. i.e., CO is a strong field ligand causes rearrangement and pairing of electrons of $3 d$ and $4 s$ orbital. Structure of $\mathrm{Ni} \left(\mathrm{CO}_4\right)$ is tetrahedral with $ s p³$ hybridisation and it is diamagnetic. Hence, (4) is the correct answer.$$

19929.text: In a chemical reaction i.e., $A+2 B \longrightarrow$ products, when concentration of $A$ is doubled, rate of the reaction increases 4 times and when concentration of $B$ alone is doubled rate continues to be the same. The order of the reaction is
19929.sol:
Let the order of reaction w.r.t. $A$ is $x$ and w.r.t. $B$ is $y$.
$r_{1}=k[A]^{x}[B]^{y} \quad \text{...(i)}r_{2}=k[2 A]^{x}[B]^{y} \quad \text{...(ii)}r_{3}=k[A]^{x}[2 B]^{y} \quad \text{...(iii)}\begin{aligned} \frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}} &=\frac{k[A]^{x}[B]^{y}}{k[2 A]^{x}[B]^{y}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x} \\ \Rightarrow \quad\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2} &=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x &=2 \end{aligned}$
Similarly,

$\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{r_{1}}{r_{3}}=\frac{k[A]^{x}[B]^{y}}{k[A]^{x}[2 B]^{y}} \Rightarrow$1=$\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{y}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad$\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{0}$&=$\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{y}$\\
y &=0
\end{aligned}

Hence,$ the rate of equation is\text{ Rate }=$k[A]^{2}[B]^{0}

Order of reaction $=2$

20073.subject: Chemistry
options: Ionic compounds of $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ are coloured because of $\mathrm{d}-\mathrm{d}$ electronic transitions

The order in which the paramagnetic nature of the 4 cations $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}, \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}, \mathrm{V}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ vary is $\mathrm{V}^{2+} < \mathrm{Cr}^{2+}=\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} < \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$
The metal Cobalt has the electronic configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{ d}^5$ in the +3 oxidation state
As the oxidation number of the transition element increases, the ionic nature decreases and the oxides show acidic nature predominantly
20073.sol:
(1) Incorrect: $Sc^{3+}$ has $[Ar]3d^0$ and $Cu^+$ has $[Ar]3d^{10}$. With completely empty or completely filled $d$-orbitals, $d$-$d$ transitions are not possible. Their compounds are colourless.

(2) Incorrect: Paramagnetism depends on number of unpaired electrons $n$.
$V^{2+}(3d^3) \to n=3$, $Cr^{2+}(3d^4) \to n=4$, $Mn^{2+}(3d^5) \to n=5$, $Fe^{2+}(3d^6) \to n=4$
Correct order: $V^{2+} < Cr^{2+} = Fe^{2+} < Mn^{2+}$

(3) Incorrect: Co is $[Ar]3d^74s^2$. In $+3$ state (Co^{3+}$), it loses 2$ electrons from $4s$ and $1$ from $3d$, giving $[Ar]3d^6$, not $3d^5$.

(4) Correct: By Fajans' rules, higher oxidation state increases polarizing power, increasing covalent character and decreasing ionic nature. Higher covalent character in oxides leads to predominantly acidic nature (e.g., $CrO_3$, $Mn_2O_7$ are acidic while $MnO$, $CrO$ are basic).

The correct statement is (4).

20129.subject: Chemistry
20129.text:
Identify the two statements which are incorrect regarding Corrosion of Iron.
A. During electrical protection of underground Iron pipes from corrosion the connected Mg plate undergoes reduction.
B. At the Cathodic area on Iron the reaction occurring is $4 \mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{O}_2+4 \mathrm{e} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
C. Rust formed $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3. \mathrm{xH}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is an acidic oxide.
D. The $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ ions are obtained from water containing dissolved gases like $\mathrm{SO}_2, \mathrm{NO}_2$ or $\mathrm{CO}_2$.
20129.sol:
In the process of cathodic protection of iron pipes, a more reactive metal like magnesium is used as a sacrificial anode. The magnesium undergoes oxidation (Mg \rightarrow Mg^{2+} + 2e^{-}$) to protect the iron. Therefore, statement A is incorrect because Mg undergoes oxidation, not reduction.

At the cathodic area of iron corrosion, oxygen is reduced in the presence of moisture. The reaction is $O_2 + 4H^{+} + 4e^{-} \rightarrow 2H_2O$. This is a standard cathodic reaction in acidic or neutral media, making statement B correct.

Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, \mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 \cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$. Iron(III) oxide is a basic oxide, not an acidic oxide. Therefore, statement C is incorrect.

The presence of dissolved acidic gases like $\mathrm{SO}_2$, $\mathrm{NO}_2$, or $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in water increases the concentration of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ ions, which accelerates the corrosion process. Thus, statement D is correct.

Since statements A and C are incorrect, the correct option is A & C.

Answer: A & C

20226.subject: Chemistry
20226.text: The best method for the separation of $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol from their mixture is:
20226.sol:
$o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol can be separated by steam distillation based on the difference in their volatility.

$o$-nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding, which reduces its intermolecular forces of attraction, making it more volatile and capable of being steam distilled.

$p$-nitrophenol exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding, leading to the formation of associated molecules, which significantly increases its boiling point and makes it less volatile.

Therefore, $o$-nitrophenol distills over with steam while $p$-nitrophenol remains in the distillation flask.

Answer: Steam distillation

20373.subject: Chemistry
20373.text:
Arrange the given alkanes in increasing order of their boiling points.
(A) 2, 2-dimethylpropane
(B) 2-methylbutane
(C) $n$-pentane
(D) $n$-butane
20373.sol:
The boiling point of alkanes increases with an increase in molecular mass due to stronger van der Waals forces. Since $n$-butane (D) has four carbon atoms while the others have five, it has the lowest boiling point.

For isomeric alkanes, the boiling point decreases with an increase in branching. Branching makes the molecule more spherical, which decreases the surface area of contact and weakens the intermolecular van der Waals forces.

Among the isomers of pentane, $n$-pentane (C) is unbranched and has the highest surface area, resulting in the highest boiling point. 2-methylbutane (B) has one branch, and 2,2-dimethylpropane (A) has two branches, making it the most spherical with the lowest boiling point among the isomers.

Thus, the increasing order of boiling points is $n$-butane (D) < 2,2-dimethylpropane (A) < 2-methylbutane (B) $< n$-pentane (C).

The correct sequence is $D < A < B < C$.

Answer: $D < A < B < C$

20450.text: $A buffer solution was prepared by mixing 5 g of acetic acid with 7.5 g of sodium acetate. The solution was made upto 500 mL. The pH of the resulting solution is:  \left[p K_a=4.76\right]$
20450.sol:
The molar mass of acetic acid ($CH_{3}COOH$) is $60\text{ g/mol}$. The number of moles of acetic acid is $n_{acid} = \dfrac{5}{60} = \dfrac{1}{12}\text{ mol}$.

The molar mass of sodium acetate ($CH_{3}COONa$) is $82\text{ g/mol}$. The number of moles of sodium acetate is $n_{salt} = \dfrac{7.5}{82} \approx 0.09146\text{ mol}$.

Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer: $pH = pK_{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{[salt]}{[acid]} \right).

Since the volume is the same for both components in the 500\text{ mL} solution, the ratio of concentrations is equal to the ratio of moles: $ pH = pK_{a} + $\log\left( \dfrac{n_{salt}}{n_{acid}} \right)$.

$pH = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{7.5/82}{5/60} \right) = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{7.5}{82} \times \dfrac{60}{5} \right) = 4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{1.5 \times 60}{82} \right) =4.76 + \log \left( \dfrac{90}{82} \right).

$ pH = 4.76 + $\log$$(1.0976) $\approx4.76 + 0.04 = 4.8$.

Answer: 4.8$

20564.subject: Chemistry
20564.text: Which of the following gas readily de-colourises the acidified $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ solution?
20564.sol: Acidified potassium permanganate ($\mathrm{KMnO}_4$) is a strong oxidizing agent. It reacts with reducing agents to get reduced, resulting in the loss of its characteristic purple color. Among the given gases, $\mathrm{SO}_2$ acts as a strong reducing agent. The reaction is as follows: $5\mathrm{SO}_2 + 2\mathrm{KMnO}_4 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 + 2\mathrm{MnSO}_4 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$ In this reaction, the oxidation state of sulfur increases from $+4$ to $+6$, and the oxidation state of manganese decreases from $+7$ to $+2$. The formation of colorless $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ ions leads to the de-colourisation of the solution. $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{P}_2\mathrm{O}_5$ are acidic oxides that do not act as reducing agents in this context. $\mathrm{NO}_2$ can act as a reducing agent in some conditions, but $\mathrm{SO}_2$ is the standard gas known for readily de-colourising acidified $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ solution. Answer: $\mathrm{SO}_2$

20957.text: A triangular park is enclosed on two sides by a fence and on the third side by a straight river bank. The two sides having fence are of same length $x$. The maximum area enclosed by the park is
20957.sol:
Let the two sides of the triangular park having fence be $x$ and $x$. Let the angle between these two sides be $\theta$.

The area $A$ of the triangle is given by the formula $A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times x \times x \times \sin(\theta) = \dfrac{1}{2} x^2 \sin(\theta)$.

To maximize the area $A$, we need to maximize $\sin(\theta)$.

The maximum value of $\sin(\theta)$ is $1$, which occurs when $\theta = 90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Substituting $\sin(\theta) = 1$ into the area formula, we get $A_\max = \dfrac{1}{2} x^2 (1) = \dfrac{1}{2} x^2$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2} x^2$

Given $y = \sin^{-1} \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x+1}}\right).

Let $ u = $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x+1}}. Then $ y = \sin^{-1}(u)$.

Using the chain rule, \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dy}{du} \times \dfrac{du}{dx}.

\dfrac{dy}{du} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{x+1}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\dfrac{x+1-1}{x+1}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{x+1}{x}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x+1}}{\sqrt{x}}.

Now, $ u = (x+1)^{-1/2}$.

\dfrac{du}{dx} = -\dfrac{1}{2}($ x+1)^{-3/2} = $-\dfrac{1}{2(x+1)\sqrt{x+1}}.

Multiplying these results:

\dfrac{dy}{dx} =\dfrac{\sqrt{x+1}}{\sqrt{x}} \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{2(x+1)\sqrt{x+1}}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}(x+1)}.$

Answer: $-\dfrac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}(1+x)}$

The sum of probabilities in a probability distribution is equal to 1.

$\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{3}{25} + K + \dfrac{1}{25} + \dfrac{1}{25} = 1$

The expected value $E(X)$ is given by $\sum x_i P(x_i)$.

$E(X) = 1 \times \dfrac{1}{2} + 2 \times \dfrac{1}{5} + 4 \times \dfrac{3}{25} + 2A \times K + 3A \times \dfrac{1}{25} + 5A \times \dfrac{1}{25} = 2.94$

$\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{2}{5} + \dfrac{12}{25} + 2A \times \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{3A}{25} + \dfrac{5A}{25} = 2.94$

$\dfrac{25 + 20 + 24}{50} + \dfrac{A}{5} + \dfrac{8A}{25} = 2.94$

$\dfrac{69}{50} + \dfrac{5A + 8A}{25} = 2.94$

$1.38 + \dfrac{13A}{25} = 2.94$

$\dfrac{13A}{25} = 2.94 - 1.38 = 1.56$

$13A = 1.56 \times 25 = 39$

$A = \dfrac{39}{13} = 3$

22388.subject: Physics
22388.text: What should be the inductance of an inductor connected to $200 \mathrm{ V}, 50 \mathrm{ Hz}$ source so that the maximum current of $\sqrt{2} A flows through it?$
22388.sol:
The root mean square voltage is given as $V_{rms} = 200 \text{ V}$. The maximum current is given as $I_\max = \sqrt{2} \text{ A}$.

The root mean square current is $I_{rms} = \dfrac{I_\max}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 1 \text{ A}$.

The inductive reactance $X_L$ is given by $X_L = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}} = \dfrac{200}{1} = 200 \Omega$.

The formula for inductive reactance is $X_L = \omega L = 2 \pi f L$, where $f = 50 \text{ Hz}$.

Substituting the values: $200 = 2 \times \pi \times 50 \times L$.

$200 = 100 \pi L$.

$L = \dfrac{200}{100 \pi} = \dfrac{2}{\pi} \text{ H}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{\pi} \mathrm{H}$

24330.text: The three numbers: (number of protons, number of neutrons, the radius) characterize a nucleus. What is the value of $\dfrac{r_1}{r_2}$ for two nuclei characterized by $(1, 0, r_1)$ and $(4, 4, r_2)$?
24330.sol:
The mass number $A$ of a nucleus is the sum of the number of protons and the number of neutrons.

For the first nucleus, $A_1 = 1 + 0 = 1$.

For the second nucleus, $A_2 = 4 + 4 = 8$.

The radius of a nucleus is given by $r = R_0 A^{1/3}$.

Therefore, the ratio of their radii is $\dfrac{r_1}{r_2} = \left(\dfrac{A_1}{A_2}\right)^{1/3}$.

Substituting the values, $\dfrac{r_1}{r_2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right)^{1/3} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

26268.text: Two spherical planets $P and Q$ have the same uniform density $\rho$, masses $M_{P} and M_{Q}$ and surface areas $A$ and 4A respectively. A spherical planet $R$ also has uniform density $\rho$ and its mass is $\left(M_{P}+M_{Q}\right)$. The escape velocities from the planets $P, Q and R$ are $V_{P}, V_{Q} and V_{R}$, respectively. Then
26268.sol:
Here Planets $P$ and $Q$ have the same uniform density ' $\rho$ ' and surface areas $A$ and $4 A$ respectively. Let the mass of $P, M_{P}$ be $m$.

Then $m=\rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}=\rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi\left[\frac{A}{4 \pi}\right]^{3 / 2}$

The mass of $M_{Q}=\rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi\left[\frac{4 A}{4 \pi}\right]^{3 / 2}=8 \mathrm{~m}$

$\therefore \quad$ The mass of Planet $R=8 \mathrm{~m}+\mathrm{m}=9 \mathrm{~m}$

If the radius of $P=r$

Then the radius of $Q=2 r$

$\left[\because r_{Q}=\left(\frac{4 A}{4 \pi}\right)^{3 / 2}=2\left(\frac{A}{4 \pi}\right)^{3 / 2}\right]$

and radius of $R=9^{1 / 3} r$

$\left[\begin{array}{l}

\because M_{R}=M_{P}+M_{Q} \\

r_{R}^{3}=r^{3}+(2 r)^{3}=9 r^{3}

\end{array}\right]$

As we know, escape velocity from the planet

$\begin{aligned} V_{e}=\sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{R}} & \therefore v_{P}=\sqrt{\frac{2 G M_{P}}{R_{p}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 G m}{r}} \\ v_{Q} &=\sqrt{\frac{2 G M_{Q}}{R_{Q}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 G(8 \mathrm{~m})}{2 r}}=2 v_{P} \\ v_{R} &=\sqrt{\frac{2 G(9 \mathrm{~m})}{9^{1 / 3} r}}=9^{1 / 3} v_{P} \end{aligned}$

26764.text: A stationary source emits sound of frequency ${f}_{0} = 492Hz$ . The sound is reflected by a large car approaching the source with a speed of $2m{s}^{- 1}$ . The reflected signal is received by the source and superposed with the original. What will be the beat frequency of the resulting signal in Hz? 26764.sol:
Frequency of sound as received by large car approaching the source.

${f}_{1} = \dfrac{C + {V}_{0}}{C}{f}_{0} = \left(\dfrac{330 + 2}{330}\right)492Hz .$

This car now acts as source for reflected sound wave

$∴ {f}_{reflected} = {f}_{1}$

Frequency of sound received by source,

${f}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{C}{C - {V}_{0}}\right){f}_{reflected} = \left(\dfrac{330}{330 - 2}\right) × {f}_{1} = \dfrac{330}{328} × \dfrac{332}{330} × 492Hz$

$∴$ Beat frequency $= \left|{f}_{0} - {f}_{2}\right| = \left(\dfrac{332}{328} - 1\right) × 492Hz$

$= 6Hz$

Firstly, car will be treated as an observer which is approaching the source. Then, it will be treated as a source, which is moving in the direction of sound.
Hence, $\quad f_1=f_0\left(\frac{v+v_1}{v-v_1}\right)$ $$ \begin{aligned} f_2 & =f_0\left(\frac{v+v_2}{v-v_2}\right) \\ \therefore \quad f_1-f_2 & =\left(\frac{1.2}{100}\right) f_0 \\ & =f_0\left[\frac{v+v_1}{v-v_1}-\frac{v+v_2}{v-v_2}\right] \\ \text{ or }\left(\frac{1.2}{100}\right) f_0 & =\frac{2 v\left(v_1-v_2\right)}{\left(v-v_1\right)\left(v-v_2\right)} f_0 \end{aligned} $$ As $v_1$ and $v_2$ are very very less than $v$. We can write, $\left(v-v_1\right)$ or $\left(v-v_2\right) \approx v$ $$ \therefore \quad\left(\frac{1.2}{100}\right) f_0=\frac{2\left(v_1-v_2\right)}{v} f_0 $$ or $\left(v_1-v_2\right)=\frac{v \times 1.2}{200}$ $$ \begin{aligned} & =\frac{330 \times 1.2}{200}=1.98 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1} \\ & =7.128 \mathrm{kmh}^{-1} \end{aligned} $$ $\therefore$ The nearest integer is 7 . Hence, $\quad f_1=f_0\left(\frac{v+v_1}{v-v_1}\right)$ $$ \begin{aligned} f_2 & =f_0\left(\frac{v+v_2}{v-v_2}\right) \\ \therefore \quad f_1-f_2 & =\left(\frac{1.2}{100}\right) f_0 \\ & =f_0\left[\frac{v+v_1}{v-v_1}-\frac{v+v_2}{v-v_2}\right] \\ \text{ or }\left(\frac{1.2}{100}\right) f_0 & =\frac{2 v\left(v_1-v_2\right)}{\left(v-v_1\right)\left(v-v_2\right)} f_0 \end{aligned} $$ As $v_1$ and $v_2$ are very very less than $v$. We can write, $\left(v-v_1\right)$ or $\left(v-v_2\right) \approx v$ $$ \therefore \quad\left(\frac{1.2}{100}\right) f_0=\frac{2\left(v_1-v_2\right)}{v} f_0 $$ or $\left(v_1-v_2\right)=\frac{v \times 1.2}{200}$ $$ \begin{aligned} & =\frac{330 \times 1.2}{200}=1.98 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1} \\ & =7.128 \mathrm{kmh}^{-1} \end{aligned} $$ $\therefore$ The nearest integer is 7 .

28919.subject: Chemistry
28919.text: The theory that can completely/properly explain the nature of bonding in $\left[Ni{\left(CO\right)$}_{4}\right]$ is:$
28919.sol:
There is synergic bonding present in $\left[Ni{\left(CO\right)}_{4}\right]$.

As $CO$ is neutral ligand, so oxidation state of nickel is zero i.e.${Ni}^{0}$.

So, electronic configuration of ${Ni}^{0}$ $= \left[Ar\right]3{d}^{8}4{s}^{2}$

As $CO$ is strong field ligand, it will back paired the 4s electrons to $3d$ orbitals.

So in complex electronic configuration of ${Ni}^{0}$ $= \left[Ar\right]3{d}^{10}4{s}^{0}$ here inner d orbital is filled.

In ligand $CO$ (carbonyl) the anti-bonding orbital is vacant.

$CO: \sigma1{s}^{2}, \sigma * 1{s}^{2}, \sigma2{s}^{2}, \sigma * 2{s}^{2}, \sigma2{p}_{z}^{2}, {\pi p}_{x}^{2} = {\pi p}_{y}^{2}, \pi * {p}_{x}^{0} = \pi * {p}_{y}^{0}$

The fully filled inner d-orbital of central metal atom gives it's electrons to vacant $\pi$ anti-bonding orbital, this is called back $\pi$ bonding, due to this back bonding bond between metal and ligand is very strong.

This back $\pi$ bonding is also called synergic bonding and this synergic bonding is explained by molecular orbital theory.

Carbon monoxide $CO$ made synergic bonding with Haemoglobin in are blood, as synergic bonding is very strong, so oxygen taking capacity of haemoglobin decrease and it cause death.

29033.text:
Number of paramagnetic ions among the following d- and f-block metal ions is _______.
$Mn^{2+}, Cu^{2+}, Zn^{2+}, Yb^{2+}, Sc^{3+}, La^{3+}, Gd^{3+}, Lu^{3+}, Ti^{4+}, Ce^{4+}$
(Atomic number of $Mn = 25, Cu = 29, Zn = 30, Yb = 70, Sc = 21, La = 57, Gd = 64, Lu = 71, Ti = 22, Ce = 58$)
29033.sol:
The magnetic nature of an ion depends on the presence of unpaired electrons. Ions with at least one unpaired electron are paramagnetic, while those with all paired electrons are diamagnetic.

Let us write the electronic configurations of the given ions:

$Mn^{2+} (Z=25) : [Ar] 3d^5$ $\rightarrow$ $5$ unpaired electrons (Paramagnetic)
$Cu^{2+} (Z=29) : [Ar] 3d^9$ $\rightarrow$ $1$ unpaired electron (Paramagnetic)
$Zn^{2+} (Z=30) : [Ar] 3d^{10}$ $\rightarrow$ $0$ unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
$Yb^{2+} (Z=70) : [Xe] 4f^{14}$ $\rightarrow$ $0$ unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
$Sc^{3+} (Z=21) : [Ar] 3d^0$ $\rightarrow$ $0$ unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
$La^{3+} (Z=57) : [Xe] 4f^0$ $\rightarrow$ $0$ unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
$Gd^{3+} (Z=64) : [Xe] 4f^7$ $\rightarrow$ $7$ unpaired electrons (Paramagnetic)
$Lu^{3+} (Z=71) : [Xe] 4f^{14}$ $\rightarrow$ $0$ unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
$Ti^{4+} (Z=22) : [Ar] 3d^0$ $\rightarrow$ $0$ unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)
$Ce^{4+} (Z=58) : [Xe] 4f^0$ $\rightarrow$ $0$ unpaired electrons (Diamagnetic)

The paramagnetic ions are $Mn^{2+}$, $Cu^{2+}$, and $Gd^{3+}$.

Total number of paramagnetic ions = $3$.

Answer: $3$

29795.text: Highest enol content will be shown by :
29795.sol:
When keto form loses a proton from the alpha carbon, it goes to the enol form. Depending on whether the proton is lost from oxygen or carbon, this conjugate acid can deliver either the carbonyl form or the enol form. 

In this case, after enolisation, it forms an aromatic compound.

Aromatic compounds are stable due to their aromaticity. The resonance stabilisation resulting from delocalised pi electrons distributes the charge over the entire ring, reducing the overall energy of the compound.

Hence, the answer is option B.

What volume of hydrogen gas at STP would be liberated by action of $50\text{ mL}$ of $H_2SO_4$ of $50\%$ purity (density $= 1.3\text{ g mL}^{-1}$) on $20\text{ g}$ of zinc ?

31864.sol:
Mass of $H_2SO_4$ solution $= 50 \times 1.3 = 65\text{ g}$

Mass of pure $H_2SO_4 = 65 \times \dfrac{50}{100} = 32.5\text{ g}$

Moles of $H_2SO_4 = \dfrac{32.5}{98} \approx 0.3316\text{ mol}$

Moles of $Zn = \dfrac{20}{65} \approx 0.3077\text{ mol}$

The balanced chemical equation is:
$Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2$

Since the moles of $Zn$ are less than the moles of $H_2SO_4$, $Zn$ is the limiting reagent.

Moles of $H_2$ produced $=$ Moles of $Zn = \dfrac{20}{65}\text{ mol}$

Volume of $H_2$ gas at STP $= \dfrac{20}{65} \times 22.4\text{ L} = 6.892\text{ L}$

Answer: $6.892\text{ L}$

33358.text:
Among the statements :

$( S1 ) : {2023}^{2022} - {1999}^{2022}$ is divisible by $8$.

$( S2 ) : 13 ( 13{)}^{n} - 11n - 13$ is divisible by $144$ for infinitely many $n \in \mathbb{N}$
33358.sol:
Given,

$( S1 ) : ( 2023{)}^{2022} - ( 1999{)}^{2022}$ is divisible by $8$

Now we know that $( x - y )$ divides $\left({x}^{n} - {y}^{n}\right) ∀ n \in \mathbb{N}$

So, $\left(2023 - 1999\right)$ divides $( 2023{)}^{2022} - ( 1999{)}^{2022}$

$⇒ 24$ divides $( 2023{)}^{2022} - ( 1999{)}^{2002}$

$⇒ 8$ will divide $( 2023{)}^{2022} - ( 1999{)}^{2002}$

As $8$ divides $24$

Hence, $\left(S1\right)$ is correct

Now solving,

$\left(S2\right): 13{\left(13\right)}^{n} - 11n - 13$ is divisible by $144$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

So using binomial theorem in ${\left(1 + 12\right)}^{n}$ we get,

$13{\left(1 + 12\right)}^{n} - 11n - 13$

$= 13\left({}^{n}{C}_{0}{+}^{n}{C}_{1}12{+}^{n}{C}_{2}{12}^{2} + . . . {+}^{n}{C}_{n}{12}^{n}\right) - 11n - 13$

$= 12 \times 13n - 11n + {12}^{2}\lambda$

$= 145n + 144\lambda$ which is not divisible by $144$

Hence, $\left(S2\right)$ is incorrect

34398.text:
Statement - I : The value of the integral $\mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{dx}{1 + \sqrt{tanx}}$ is equal to $\dfrac{\pi}{6} .$

Statement - II : $\mathop{∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = \mathop{∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx .$
options: Statement - $I$ is true; Statement - $II$ is false.
Statement - $I$ is false; Statement - $II$ is true.
Statement - $I$ true; Statement - $II$ is true; Statement - $II$ is a correct explanation for Statement - $I$.
Statement - $I$ is true; Statement - $II$ is true; Statement - $II$ is not a correct explanation for Statement - $I$.
34398.sol:
Statement $II$ is a standard property of definite integrals.

For statement $I$ : $I = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{dx}{1 + \sqrt{tanx}} = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{dx}{1 + \sqrt{cotx}}$

$I = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{\sqrt{tanx}}{1 + \sqrt{tanx}}dx = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{\sqrt\sinx}{\sqrt\cosx + \sqrt{sinx}}dx = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{\sqrt\cosx}{\sqrt\cosx + \sqrt{sinx}}dx$

$2I = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}dx$

$2I = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$I = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$

Hence, statement $I$ is false.

36727.text: A player $X$ has a biased coin whose probability of showing heads is $p$ and a player $Y$ has a fair coin. They start playing a game with their own coins and play alternately. 36727.sol:
If the outcome is one of the following: $H, T T H, T T T T H, \ldots$, then $X$ wins As subsequent tosses are independent, so the probability that $X$ wins is

p+$\frac{p}{4}+\frac{p}{16}+\ldots=\frac{4 p}{3} .$Similarly $Y$ wins if the outcome is one of the following: $T H, T T T H, T T T T T H, \ldots$
Therefore, the probability that $Y$ wins is

$\frac{1-p}{2}+\frac{1-p}{8}+\frac{1-p}{32}=\frac{2(1-p)}{3}$Since, the probability of winning the game by both the players is equal then, we have

$\frac{4 p}{3}=\frac{2(1-p)}{3} \Rightarrow$p=$\frac{1}{3}$

39599.text: Wheatstone bridge principle is used to measure the specific resistance $\left({S}_{1}\right)$ of given wire, having length $L$, radius $r$. If $X$ is the resistance of wire, then specific resistance is : ${S}_{1} = X \left(\dfrac{\pi{r}^{2}}{L}\right). If the length of the wire gets doubled then the value of specific resistance will be :$
39599.sol:
The specific resistance of a material, also known as electrical resistivity, is a measure of how strongly a specific material opposes the flow of electric current.

Specific resistance is an intrinsic property of a material and is dependent on factors such as the material's composition, temperature, and crystal structure. It is the counterpart of conductivity, with which it is inversely proportional.

Hence, even if the length of the wire is doubled, the specific resistance remains the same, i.e., ${S}_{1}$.

Let resistance of potentiometers wire is $R$, then the current through $AB$

${i}_{AB} = \dfrac{4}{R + 780}$

Potential difference across $AB$

${V}_{AB} = \dfrac{4R}{R + 780}$

Potential difference across $AC$

${V}_{AC} = {V}_{AB}\dfrac{l}{L} = \dfrac{4R}{\left(R + 780\right)} \times \dfrac{60}{300} = \dfrac{4R}{5\left(R + 780\right)}$

This should be equal to $20mV$

$⇒ \dfrac{4R}{5\left(R + 780\right)} = 20 \times {10}^{- 3} = 2 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$⇒ 4R = {10}^{- 1}\left(R + 780\right)$

$⇒ 4R - \dfrac{R}{10} = 78$

$⇒ \dfrac{39R}{10} = 78$

$⇒ R = 20Ω$

40686.text:
A spherically symmetric charge distribution is characterised by a charge density having the following variations:
$\rho(r)=\rho_o\left(1-\frac{r}{R}\right)$ for $r < R$
$\rho(\mathrm{r})=0$ for $r \geq \mathrm{R}$
Where $r$ is the distance from the centre of the charge distribution $\rho_{\mathrm{o}}$ is a constant. The electric field at an internal point $(r < R)$ is:
40686.sol:
Let us consider a spherical shell of radius $x$ and thickness $\mathrm{dx}$.
Charge on this shell $$ d q=\rho .4 \pi x^2 d x=\rho_0\left(1-\frac{x}{R}\right) \cdot 4 \pi x^2 d x $$ $\therefore$ Total charge in the spherical region from centre to $r(r < R)$ is $$ \begin{aligned} &q=\int d q=4 \pi \rho_0 \int_0^r\left(1-\frac{x}{R}\right) x^2 d x \\ &=4 \pi \rho_0\left[\frac{x^3}{3}-\frac{x^4}{4 R}\right]_0^r \\ &=4 \pi \rho_0\left[\frac{r^3}{3}-\frac{r^4}{4 R}\right] \\ &=4 \pi \rho_0 r^3\left[\frac{1}{3}-\frac{r}{4 R}\right] \end{aligned} $$ $\therefore$ Electric field at $\mathrm{r}, \mathrm{E}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{q}}{\mathrm{r}^2}$ $$ \begin{aligned} &=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{4 \pi \rho_0 r^3}{r^2}\left[\frac{1}{3}-\frac{r}{4 R}\right] \\ &=\frac{\rho_0}{\varepsilon_0}\left[\frac{r}{3}-\frac{r^2}{4 R}\right] \end{aligned} $$

40900.text: An object is taken to a height above the surface of earth at a distance $\dfrac{5}{4}R$ from the centre of the earth. Where radius of earth, $R = 6400km$. The percentage decrease in the weight of the object will be
40900.sol:
Acceleration due to gravity at height $h$ is given by, ${g}^{'} = \dfrac{g}{{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)}^{2}}$

For distance from the centre $r = \dfrac{5}{4}R$ height $h = \dfrac{R}{4}$,

$⇒ {g}^{'} = \dfrac{g}{{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{16}{25}g$

Change in weight

$∆ W = mg - m{g}^{'} ⇒ ∆ W = mg\left(1 - \dfrac{16}{25}\right)$

$⇒ ∆ W = \dfrac{9}{25}mg$

Percentage change $= \dfrac{9}{25} \times 100 %$

$= 36 %$

Total volume of rain drops, received $100 \mathrm{~cm}$ in a year by area $1 \mathrm{~m}^2$
=1 $\mathrm{~m}^$2 $\times \frac{100}{100} \mathrm{~m}=$1 $\mathrm{~m}^$3

As we know, density of water,

d=10^3 $\mathrm{~kg}$/ $\mathrm{m}^$3

Therefore, mass of this volume of water $M=d \times v=10^3 \times 1=10^3 \mathrm{~kg}$
Average terminal velocity of rain drop $v=9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ (given)
Therefore, energy transferred by rain,

$\begin{aligned}$&E=$\frac{1}{2}$m v² \\
&=$\frac{1}{2} \times$10^3 $\times($9)^2 \\
&=$\frac{1}{2} \times$10^3 $\times$81=4.05 $\times$10^4 $\mathrm{~J}
\end{aligned}$

42105.text: Two metallic wires $P$ and $Q$ have same volume and are made up of same material. If their area of cross sections are in the ratio $4: 1$ and force ${F}_{1}$ is applied to $P$, an extension of $∆ l$ is produced. The force which is required to produce same extension in $Q$ is ${F}_{2}$. The value of $\dfrac{{F}_{1}}{{F}_{2}}$ is ______.
42105.sol:
The formula for Young's modulus is given by

$\begin{cases}Y & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{∆ l}{l}} \\ & = & \dfrac{Fl}{A ∆ l}\end{cases}$

From above equation, it follows that

$\Deltal = \dfrac{Fl}{AY} . . . \left(1\right)$

Again, volume of the wire is given by

$V = Al ⇒ l = \dfrac{V}{A}$

Hence, from equation (1),

$∆ l = \dfrac{FV}{{A}^{2}Y} . . . \left(2\right)$

As, $Y$ and $V$ is the same for both the wires,

$∆ l ∝ \dfrac{F}{{A}^{2}}$

Hence, for two wires, it can be written that

$\dfrac{∆ {l}_{1}}{∆ {l}_{2}} = \dfrac{{F}_{1}}{{A}_{1}^{2}} \times {A}_{2}^{2}{F}_{2} . . . \left(3\right)$

As $∆ {l}_{1} = ∆ {l}_{2}$, from equation (3), it follows that

${F}_{1}{A}_{2}^{2} = {F}_{2}{A}_{1}^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{{F}_{1}}{{F}_{2}} = {A}_{1}^{2}{A}_{2}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{4}{1}\right)}^{2} = 16$

42689.text: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude $A$. Its speed is increased to three times at an instant when its displacement is $\dfrac{2A}{3}$. The new amplitude of motion is $\dfrac{nA}{3}$. The value of $n$ is _____.
42689.sol:
Speed in SHM in terms of displacement is given by, $v = \omega\sqrt{{A}^{2} - {x}^{2}}$.

at $x = \dfrac{2A}{3}$, we get

$v = \omega\sqrt{{A}^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{2A}{3}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}A\omega}{3}$

Let the new amplitude be$= A '$

Then, 

$v ' = 3v ⇒ \omega\sqrt{{\left(A '\right)}^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{2A}{3}\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{5}A\omega$

$⇒ A ' = \dfrac{7}{3}A$

Therefore, $n = 7$.

44798.subject: Botany
44798.sol: Turbellaria (L. turbella - a string) is a class of phylum-Platyhelminthes. Turbellarians are mostly free, living flat worms, majorly aquatic (marine), presence of cilia, body unsegmented, mouth ventral, suckers absent with tango, chemo and photoreceptors, eg, Planaria (Dugesia), Bipalium etc. Trematoda (Gr. trema = hole; eidos $=$ form), class of phylum-Platyhelminthes. Commonly called 'flukes', ecto or endoparasites, body without cilia, unsegmented with suckers and hooks, eg, Fasciola, Schistosoma etc.Cestoda (Gr. kestos $=$ girdle eidos $=$ form) is also one of the class of phylum-Platyhelminthes. They are commonly called 'tapeworms' parasites without cilia and sense organs body segmented (pseudometamerism), digestive system absent, eg, Taenia and Echinococcus.

45080.subject: Botany
45080.text:
Which of the following characteristics is are exhibited by $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants?
I. Kranz anatomy.
II. The first product of photosynthesis is oxaloacetic acid.
III. Both PEP carboxylates and ribulose biphosphate carboxylate act as carboxylating enzymes.
The correct option is
options: I and III, but not II
I and II, but not III
II and III, but not I
45080.sol:
$\mathrm{C}_4$-plants have an alternative $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation pathway called Hatch and Slack cycle. These plants have Kranz anatomy in leaf, where vascular bundles are surrounded by bundle sheath.
In $\mathrm{C}_4$ cycle light reaction occurs in, mesophyll chloroplast by PEP carboxylaes and the assimilation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ takes place in, i.e., dark phase in bundle sheath chloroplast by Rubisco.

45272.subject: Botany
45272.text: Which one of the given pollination technique/adaptation is different than others?
45272.sol:
Geitonogamy is a technique of self-pollination, in which pollen of one flower is deposited on the stigma of another flower of same plant.
While others are mechanisms adopted by bisexual flowers to avoid self-pollination and promote cross-pollination.
- Dichogamy The condition where maturing time of anther and stigma is different. Anther matures first, i.e. protandry, stigma matures first, i.e. protogyny.
- Herkogamy Includes mechanical barrier in flower to ensure cross-pollination.
- Heterostyle The height of stigma and anther is different to avoid self-pollination.

46426.subject: Physics
46426.text: A metro train starts from rest and in 5 s achieves $108 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$. After that it moves with constant velocity and comes to rest after travelling 45 m with uniform retardation. If total distance travelled is 395 m, find total time of travelling.
46426.sol:
Given, $v=108 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}=30 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
For first equation of motion
$v=u+a t \therefore \quad 30=0+a \times 5 \quad(\because u=0)
or \quad a=6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$
So, distance travelled by metro train in 5 s
$s_1=\frac{1}{2} a t^2=\frac{1}{2} \times(6) \times(5)^2=75 \mathrm{~m}$
Distance travelled before coming to rest
$=45 \mathrm{~m}$
So, from third equation of motion
$\begin{aligned} & 0^2=(30)^2-2 a^{\prime} \times 45 \\ & \text{ or } \quad a^{\prime}=\frac{30 \times 30}{2 \times 45}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \\ & \end{aligned}$
Time taken in travelling 45 m is
$t_3=\frac{30}{10}=3 \mathrm{~s}$
Now, total distance $=395 \mathrm{~m}$
ie, $\quad 75+s^{\prime}+45=395 \mathrm{~m}$ or $s^{\prime}=395-(75+45)=275 \mathrm{~m}\therefore \quad t_2=\frac{275}{30}=9.2 \mathrm{~s}$
Hence, total time taken in whole journey
$\begin{aligned} & =t_1+t_2+t_3 \\ & =5+9.2+3 \\ & =17.2 \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$

46687.text: The ratio of the dimensions of Planck's constant and that of the moment of inertia is the dimension of
46687.sol:
$E=h \nu$
$\Rightarrow  h=$ Planck's constant $=\frac{E}{\mu}$
$\therefore [h]=\frac{[E]}{[\mu]}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right]}$
$=\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]$
and $I=$ moment of inertia $=M R^2$
Hence, $\frac{[h]}{[I]}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{ML}^2\right]}=\left[\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right]$
$=\frac{1}{[\mathrm{~T}]}=$ dimensions of frequency
Alternative: $\frac{h}{I}=\frac{E / \mu}{I}$
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{E \times T}{I}=\frac{\left(\mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{m}^2 / \mathrm{s}^2\right) \times \mathrm{s}}{\left(\mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{m}^2\right)} \\ & =\frac{1}{s}=\frac{1}{\text{ time }}=\text{ frequency }\end{aligned}$
Thus, dimensions of $\frac{h}{I}$ is same as of frequency.

56627.subject: Chemistry
56627.text: Which from following pair of elements in their respective oxidation states have same number of unpaired electrons ?
56627.sol:
The electronic configuration of $\text{Fe}$ ($Z=26$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6 4s^2$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$. It has $4$ unpaired electrons.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}$ ($Z=25$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5$. It has $5$ unpaired electrons.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}$ ($Z=27$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7 4s^2$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7$. It has $3$ unpaired electrons.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Ni}$ ($Z=28$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^2$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$. It has $2$ unpaired electrons.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Cr}$ ($Z=24$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^1$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4$. It has $4$ unpaired electrons.

Thus, $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ both have $4$ unpaired electrons.

Answer: $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cr}^{2+}$

57790.subject: Chemistry
57790.text:
Which of the following compounds forms
1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane when treated with HBr ?
57790.sol:
Electrophilic addition of HBr to alkenes follows Markovnikov's rule, with hydrogen adding to the carbon of the double bond with more hydrogen atoms. The product 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane has both bromine and methyl substituents on the same carbon.

1-Methylcyclohexene (Option A) reacts with HBr to form a tertiary carbocation at C1, stabilized by the methyl group and ring structure. Bromide addition yields 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane.

3-Methylcyclohexene and 4-methylcyclohexene (Options B and C) form secondary carbocations, leading to 2-bromo-3-methylcyclohexane and 2-bromo-4-methylcyclohexane, respectively.

1-Methyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene (Option D) undergoes 1,2-addition to produce unsaturated bromoalkene products.

Only Option A yields the desired product.

57951.subject: Chemistry
57951.text: There are two different solutions, A and B. The pH of solution A is 4. Find the pH of solution B having $[\text{H}^+]$ three times that of solution A.
57951.sol:
The pH of solution A is given as $4$.

$[\text{H}^+]_A = 10^{-4} \text{ M}$

For solution B, the hydrogen ion concentration is three times that of solution A.

$[\text{H}^+]_B = 3 \times [\text{H}^+]_A = 3 \times 10^{-4} \text{ M}$

$\text{pH of solution B} = -\log[\text{H}^+]_B$

$\text{pH} = -\log(3 \times 10^{-4})$

$\text{pH} = 4 - \log 3$

Using $\log 3 = 0.4771$:

$\text{pH} = 4 - 0.4771 = 3.5229$

Answer: $3.5229$

59169.subject: Chemistry
59169.text: Calculate the osmotic pressure of 0.03 mole of non electrolyte solute dissolved in $0.1 \mathrm{dm}^3$ of water at $300 \mathrm{ K}  \left[\mathrm{R}=0.0821 \mathrm{dm}^3 \mathrm{ atm} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1} \mathrm{ K}^{-1}\right]$
59169.sol:
The osmotic pressure $\Pi$ is given by the van't Hoff equation: $\Pi = iCRT$.

For a non-electrolyte, the van't Hoff factor is $i = 1$ since there is no dissociation. The molar concentration is calculated from $C = n/V = 0.03\ \text{mol} / 0.1\ \text{dm}^3 = 0.3\ \text{mol/dm}^3$.

Substituting the known values,

$\Pi = (1)(0.3\ \text{mol/dm}^3)(0.0821\ \text{dm}^3\ \text{atm}\ \text{mol}^{-1}\ \textK^{-1})(300\ \text{K}) = 7.389\ \text{atm}$.

Rounded to one decimal place, $\Pi = 7.4\ \text{atm}$, which corresponds to option A.

60270.text: The abscissae of the points of the curve $\mathrm{y}=x^3$ are in the interval $[-2,2]$, where the slope of the tangents can be obtained by mean value theorem for the interval $[-2,2]$ are
60270.sol:
Applying the Mean Value Theorem to the function $f(x) = x^3$ on the interval $[-2, 2]$:

$f(x)$ is a polynomial, hence continuous and differentiable throughout, satisfying the MVT conditions.

The derivative $f'(x) = 3x^2$, and the average rate of change is:

$\frac{f(2) - f(-2)}{2 - (-2)} = \frac{8 - (-8)}{4} = 4$

Setting $f'(c) = 4$ yields:

$3c^2 = 4$
$c^2 = \frac{4}{3}$
$c = \pm\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

Both values lie in $(-2, 2)$, giving the abscissae where the tangent slope equals the secant slope.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$

62189.subject: Mathematics
62189.text: If $\int x^2 \cdot e^x dx = e^x f(x) + c$, then the minimum value of $f(x)$ is...
62189.sol:
Using integration by parts:

$\int x^2 e^x dx = x^2 e^x - \int 2x e^x dx$

$= x^2 e^x - 2(x e^x - \int e^x dx)$

$= x^2 e^x - 2x e^x + 2e^x + c$

$= e^x (x^2 - 2x + 2) + c$

Comparing with the given expression, we get $f(x) = x^2 - 2x + 2$.

To find the minimum value of $f(x)$, we can complete the square:

$f(x) = (x - 1)^2 + 1$

Since $(x - 1)^2 \geq 0$ for all real $x$, the minimum value of $f(x)$ is $1$.

Answer: $1$

62729.text: If $\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{10^x+7^x-14^x-5^x}{1-\cos x}, x \neq 0$ is continuous at $x=0$, then the value of $f(0)$ is
62729.sol:
Evaluating the limit as $x \to 0$ for continuity gives $f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{10^x + 7^x - 14^x - 5^x}{1 - \cos x}$, an indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}$.

Factoring the numerator, $10^x + 7^x - 14^x - 5^x = (2^x - 1)(5^x - 7^x)$.

The limit simplifies using standard forms: $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{a^x - 1}{x} = \log a$ and $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{1 - \cos x}{x^2} = \frac{1}{2}$.

Multiply and divide by $x^2$: $f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{(2^x - 1)(5^x - 7^x)}{x^2} \cdot \frac{x^2}{1 - \cos x}$
First factor yields $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{2^x - 1}{x} \cdot \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{5^x - 7^x}{x} = \log 2 \cdot \log \left(\frac{5}{7}\right)
Second factor gives \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{x^2}{1 - \cos x} =2$

Combining results: $f(0) = 2 \log 2 $\cdot $\log\left(\frac{5}{7}\right) = \log4 $\cdot $\log\left(\frac{5}{7}\right)$

Applying L'Hôpital's rule twice confirms the result: $ f(0) = (\log 10)^2 + (\log 7)^2 - (\log 14)^2 - (\log 5)^2 = 2 \log 2 $\cdot $\log\left(\frac{5}{7}\right)$

The function must satisfy $ f(0) = \log 4 $\cdot $\log \ left(\frac{5}{7}\right),$ matching option B.

$$

63973.text: In a triangle ABC , with usual notations, $\cot \left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right) \cdot \tan \left(\frac{A-B}{2}\right)=$
63973.sol:
In triangle $ABC$ where $A + B + C = \pi$, the expression $\cot \left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right) \cdot \tan\left(\frac{A-B}{2}\right) simplifies as follows.

Using the angle sum property, \frac{A+B}{2} = \frac{\pi - C}{2} = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{C}{2}.
By the complementary angle identity \$ cot\$left(\frac{\pi}{2} -$ x\right) = \tan x$, we obtain:
\cot \$ left($\frac{A+B}{2}\right) = \tan\left(\frac{C}{2}\right) .

Napier's Analogy gives \tan \left(\frac{A-B}{2}\right) =\frac{a-b}{a+b} \cot \left(\frac{C}{2}\right)$.
Since \cot $\left(\frac{C}{2}\right) =\frac{1}{\tan \left(\frac{C}{2}\right)$}, this becomes:
\tan $\left(\frac{A-B}{2}\right) =\frac{a-b}{a+b} \cdot \frac{1}{\tan \left(\frac{C}{2}\right)$}.

Substituting both results into the original expression:
\tan \$ left(\frac{C}{2}\right) \cdot \left( \frac{a-b}{a+b} \cdot \frac{1}{\tan \left(\frac{C}{2}\right)} \right) = \frac{a-b}{a+b}.$

Thus, the simplified expression is $\frac{a-b}{a+b}$.$

64420.text: The lines $\frac{6 x-6}{18}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-1}{5}$ and $\frac{3 x+6}{12}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z+1}{2}$ are $\ldots$
64420.sol:
To analyze the relationship between the lines, their symmetric equations are rewritten and compared.

The first line simplifies to $\frac{x-1}{3} = \frac{y+1}{3} = \frac{z-1}{5}$, passing through $P_1(1, -1, 1)$ with direction vector $\vec{d_1} = (3, 3, 5)$.

The second line simplifies to $\frac{x+2}{4} = \frac{y-1}{3} = \frac{z+1}{2}$, passing through $P_2(-2, 1, -1)$ with direction vector $\vec{d_2} = (4, 3, 2)$.

Parallelism Check: Since $\frac{3}{4} \neq \frac{3}{3} \neq \frac{5}{2}$, the direction vectors are not proportional; the lines are not parallel.

Intersection Check: Parameterize Line 1 as $x = 3\lambda + 1$, $y = 3\lambda - 1$, $z = 5\lambda + 1$ and Line 2 as $x = 4\mu - 2$, $y = 3\mu + 1$, $z = 2\mu - 1$.
Equating $x$ and $y$ gives $3\lambda - 4\mu = -3$ and $3\lambda - 3\mu = 2$, solving to $\mu = 5$ and $\lambda = 17/3$.
Substituting into $z$ yields $55/3 = -2$, a contradiction.

As the lines are not parallel and do not intersect, they are skew.

Thus, the relationship is skew lines, and the correct option is C.

64442.subject: Mathematics
64442.text: The line passing through the points $(a, 1,6) and (3,4, b)$ crosses the yz -plane at $\left(0, \frac{17}{2}, \frac{-13}{2}\right)$, then the value of $(3 a+4 b)$ is
64442.sol:
Given: The line through $P_1 = (a, 1, 6)$ and $P_2 = (3, 4, b)$ intersects the yz-plane at $P_3 = (0, \frac{17}{2}, -\frac{13}{2})$. We determine $a$ and $b$ using the section formula.

Since $P_3$ lies on the yz-plane, its x-coordinate is zero. From the section formula:

$0 = \frac{3\lambda + a}{\lambda + 1} \implies 3\lambda + a = 0$

Using the y-coordinate:

$\frac{17}{2} = \frac{4\lambda + 1}{\lambda + 1} \implies 17\lambda + 17 = 8\lambda + 2 \implies 9\lambda = -15 \implies \lambda = -\frac{5}{3}$

Substituting into the x-coordinate relation:

$3(-\frac{5}{3}) + a = 0 \implies a = 5$

Using the z-coordinate:

$-\frac{13}{2} = \frac{-\frac{5}{3}b + 6}{-\frac{5}{3} + 1} = \frac{-\frac{5b}{3} + 6}{-\frac{2}{3}} = \frac{-5b + 18}{-2}$

Multiplying both sides by $-2$:

$-13(-2) = -5b + 18 \implies 26 = -5b + 18 \implies 5b = -8 \implies b = -\frac{8}{5}$

Therefore:

$3a + 4b = 3(5) + 4(-\frac{8}{5}) = 15 - \frac{32}{5} = \frac{43}{5}$

The final result is $\boxed{\frac{43}{5}}$.

64941.subject: Mathematics
64941.text: If $33\theta = \pi$, then the value of $\cos\theta \cos2\theta \cos4\theta \cos8\theta \cos16\theta$ is
64941.sol:
Let $P = \cos\theta \cos2\theta \cos4\theta \cos8\theta \cos16\theta$

Multiplying and dividing by $2\sin\theta$, we get:

$P = \dfrac{2\sin\theta \cos\theta \cos2\theta \cos4\theta \cos8\theta \cos16\theta}{2\sin\theta}$

Using the identity $\sin(2x) = 2\sin x \cos x$ repeatedly:

$P = \dfrac{\sin2\theta \cos2\theta \cos4\theta \cos8\theta \cos16\theta}{2\sin\theta}$

$P = \dfrac{\sin4\theta \cos4\theta \cos8\theta \cos16\theta}{4\sin\theta}$

$P = \dfrac{\sin8\theta \cos8\theta \cos16\theta}{8\sin\theta}$

$P = \dfrac{\sin16\theta \cos16\theta}{16\sin\theta}$

$P = \dfrac{\sin32\theta}{32\sin\theta}$

Given $33\theta = \pi$, we have $32\theta = \pi - \theta$

Therefore, $\sin32\theta = \sin(\pi - \theta) = \sin\theta$

Substituting this back into the expression for $P$:

$P = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{32\sin\theta} = \dfrac{1}{32}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{32}$

65146.text: If $\bar{a}, \overline{\mathrm{ b}}, \overline{\mathrm{c}}$ are three coplanar vectors such that $|\bar{a}|=1,|\overline{\mathrm{ b}}|=2, \overline{\mathrm{ b}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}=8$ and the angle between $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ then the value of $|\bar{a} \times(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})|$ is
65146.sol:
Given vectors $\bar{a}$, $\bar{b}$, and $\bar{c}$ are coplanar with magnitudes $|\bar{a}| = 1$ and $|\bar{b}| = 2$, and $\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = 8$ at a $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ angle.

The magnitude of $\bar{c}$ is determined using the dot product: $8 = 2|\bar{c}|\cos45^{{}^{\circ}}$, so $8 = 2|\bar{c}| \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}|\bar{c}|$, yielding $|\bar{c}| = \frac{8}{\sqrt{2}} = 4\sqrt{2}$.

The magnitude of the cross product is then $|\bar{b} \times \bar{c}| = 2 \cdot 4\sqrt{2} \cdot \sin45^{{}^{\circ}} = 8\sqrt{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 8$.

Since $\bar{a}$ is coplanar with $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$, it is perpendicular to $\bar{b} \times \bar{c}$, which is normal to their plane. Thus, the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b} \times \bar{c}$ is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$, and $|\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c})| = |\bar{a}||\bar{b} \times \bar{c}|\sin90^{{}^{\circ}} = 1 \cdot 8 \cdot 1 = 8$.

Answer: $8$

65571.text:
In the circuit shown, the ratio of the quality factor and the band width is
(Given: band width = R/L)
65571.sol:
The quality factor $Q$ of a series LCR circuit is given by:

$Q = \dfrac{\omega_0 L}{R}$

where $\omega_0$ is the resonant angular frequency, $\omega_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{LC}}$.

The bandwidth is given as $\Delta \omega = \dfrac{R}{L}$.

The ratio of the quality factor to the bandwidth is:

$\text{Ratio} = \dfrac{Q}{\Delta \omega} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\omega_0 L}{R}}{\dfrac{R}{L}} = \omega_0 \dfrac{L^2}{R^2}$

Substituting $\omega_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{LC}}$, we get:

$\text{Ratio} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{LC}} \dfrac{L^2}{R^2}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{LC}}\dfrac{L^2}{R^2}$

67377.text: If $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity on earth's surface, the gain of the potential energy of an object of mass $m$ raised from the surface of the earth to a height equal to the radius $R$ of the earth is
67377.sol:
The potential energy of an object at the surface of the earth U_{1}=-$\frac{G M m}{R}$ The potential energy of the object at a height $h=R$ from the surface of the earth U_{2}=-$\frac{G M m}{R+h}=-\frac{G M m}{R+R}$ Hence, the gain in potential energy of the object $\begin{aligned} \Delta$ U &=U_{2}-U_{1} \\
$\Delta$ U &=-$\frac{G M m}{R+R}+\frac{G M m}{R}$\\
$\Delta$ U &=-$\frac{G M m}{2 R}+\frac{G M m}{R}$\\
$\Delta$ U &=$\frac{1}{2} \frac{G M m}{R}
\end{aligned}$ But we know that $G M=g R^{2}$
Hence, $\Delta$ U=$\frac{1}{2} \frac{g R^{2} m}{R}$ or $\Delta$ U=$\frac{1}{2}$ g R m or $\Delta$ U=$\frac{1}{2}$ m g R

67532.subject: Physics
67532.text: The weight of man in lift moving in upward direction with an acceleration 'a' is $660$ N. When the lift moves in the downward direction with the same acceleration, his weight is found to be $380$ N. The real weight of the man when the lift is at rest is
67532.sol:
Let the mass of the man be $m$ and the acceleration of the lift be $a$.

When the lift moves upwards with acceleration $a$, the apparent weight is given by:

$W_1 = m(g + a) = 660$

When the lift moves downwards with acceleration $a$, the apparent weight is given by:

$W_2 = m(g - a) = 380$

Adding the two equations, we get:

$m(g + a) + m(g - a) = 660 + 380$

$2mg = 1040$

$mg = 520$ N

The real weight of the man when the lift is at rest is $mg = 520$ N.

Answer: $520$ N

Number of half-lives $n = \dfrac{t}{T_{1/2}} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2$

Fraction of sample remaining after $n$ half-lives is given by $\dfrac{N}{N_0} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^n$

$\dfrac{N}{N_0} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Fraction of sample decayed $= 1 - \dfrac{N}{N_0} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Percentage of fraction decayed $= \dfrac{3}{4} \times 100\% = 75\%$

Answer: $75\%$

69939.text:
Heat is supplied to a diatomic gas at constant pressure. The ratio of $\Delta \mathrm{Q}: \Delta \mathrm{U}: \Delta \mathrm{W}$ is
[Given $\rightarrow \Delta Q=$ heat supplied, $\Delta U=$ change in internal energy, $\Delta W=$ work done]
69939.sol:
For a diatomic gas at constant pressure:

The degrees of freedom are $f = 5$ (3 translational + 2 rotational), so $C_v = \frac{5}{2}R$ and $C_p = C_v + R = \frac{7}{2}R$.

Using the ideal gas law and thermodynamic relations:

$\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T = \frac{5}{2} n R \Delta T$

$\Delta W = P \Delta V = n R \Delta T$

$\Delta Q = n C_p \Delta T = \frac{7}{2} n R \Delta T = \Delta U + \Delta W$

The ratio becomes $\frac{7}{2} n R \Delta T : \frac{5}{2} n R \Delta T : n R \Delta T$. Multiplying through by 2 to eliminate fractions gives $7:5:2$.

Thus, $\Delta Q:\Delta U:\Delta W = 7:5:2$.

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

70201.subject: Physics
70201.text: In Young's double slit experiment, in an interference pattern, a minimum is observed exactly in front of one slit. The distance between the two coherent sources is d and D is the distance between source and screen. The possible wavelengths used are proportional to
70201.sol:
The distance between the coherent sources is $d$ and the distance to the screen is $D$. For a point at position $y = d/2$ directly in front of one slit, the path difference becomes $\Delta x = \frac{(d/2)d}{D} = \frac{d^2}{2D}$.

Destructive interference requires $\Delta x = (2n - 1)\frac{\lambda}{2}$ for $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$. Equating the expressions gives $\frac{d^2}{2D} = (2n - 1)\frac{\lambda}{2}$.

Simplifying yields $\lambda = \frac{d^2}{(2n - 1)D}$. The possible wavelengths are therefore proportional to $\frac{1}{D}$, $\frac{1}{3D}$, $\frac{1}{5D}$, … matching the sequence in option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

70952.subject: Biology
70952.text: Glucosinolates protect _________ plant from pest attack.
70952.sol:
Glucosinolates are a class of secondary metabolites containing sulfur and nitrogen, which are primarily found in plants of the family Brassicaceae.

When the plant tissue is damaged by pests or herbivores, glucosinolates are broken down by the enzyme myrosinase into toxic compounds such as isothiocyanates, which act as a defense mechanism against pest attack.

Among the given options, cabbage belongs to the family Brassicaceae. Therefore, glucosinolates protect cabbage plants from pest attack.

Answer: cabbage

70963.subject: Biology
70963.text: Which amino acids are synthesized from intermediates of Krebs cycle like alpha-ketoglutarate and oxaloacetate?
70963.sol:
The intermediates of the Krebs cycle serve as precursors for the synthesis of various amino acids through transamination reactions.

$\alpha$-ketoglutarate undergoes reductive amination or transamination to form glutamic acid (glutamate).

Oxaloacetate undergoes transamination, accepting an amino group from glutamate, to form aspartic acid (aspartate).

Therefore, glutamic acid and aspartic acid are the amino acids synthesized from $\alpha$-ketoglutarate and oxaloacetate, respectively.

Answer: Glutamic acid and aspartic acid

71229.text: Which of the following groups of bacteria are used in the commercial production of Yoghurt?
71229.sol:
Yoghurt is a fermented milk product produced commercially by adding a starter culture containing Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus bulgaricus to milk.

These bacteria ferment the lactose in milk to produce lactic acid, which acts on milk protein to give yoghurt its texture and characteristic tart flavor.

Propionibacterium shermanii is used in the production of Swiss cheese, Penicillium roquefortii is used for Roquefort cheese, and Acetobacter aceti is used for the production of acetic acid.

Answer: Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus bulgaricus.

71751.subject: Chemistry
71751.text: Identify the anionic sphere complex from following.
71751.sol:
An anionic sphere complex is a coordination compound in which the complex ion (coordination sphere) carries a net negative charge.

Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) is $[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]$. The net charge on the complex is $+3 + 3(0) + 3(-1) = 0$. It is a neutral complex.

Tetramminecopper(II) ion is $[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$. The net charge on the complex is $+2 + 4(0) = +2$. It is a cationic complex.

Sodium hexanitrocobaltate(III) is $Na_3[Co(NO_2)_6]$. The complex ion is $[Co(NO_2)_6]^{3-}$. The net charge on the complex sphere is $+3 + 6(-1) = -3$. It is an anionic complex.

Pentacarbonyliron(0) is $[Fe(CO)_5]$. The net charge on the complex is $0 + 5(0) = 0$. It is a neutral complex.

Therefore, Sodium hexanitrocobaltate(III) contains an anionic coordination sphere.

Answer: Sodium hexanitrocobaltate(III)

71862.subject: Chemistry
71862.text: Which of the following buffer solutions is used for precipitation of cations of the III A group?
71862.sol:
In qualitative analysis, the cations of group III A (such as $\text{Fe}^{3+}$, $\text{Al}^{3+}$, and $\text{Cr}^{3+}$) are precipitated as their hydroxides.

The group reagent used for this purpose is a mixture of ammonium hydroxide ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) and ammonium chloride ($\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$).

The addition of $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ suppresses the ionization of the weak base $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ due to the common ion effect. This maintains a low concentration of hydroxide ions ($\text{OH}^{-}$), which is just sufficient to exceed the solubility product ($K_{sp}$) of group III A hydroxides and precipitate them, while preventing the precipitation of hydroxides of subsequent groups which have higher $K_{sp}$ values.

Thus, the buffer solution used is $\text{NH}_4\text{OH} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ in water.

Answer: $\text{NH}_4\text{OH} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ in water.

71954.subject: Chemistry
71954.text: A solid is formed of two different elements, A and B. In this atoms of A are arranged in the CCP array, and atoms of B occupy all octahedral voids and half of tetrahedral voids. Find the formula of the solid.
71954.sol:
In a CCP lattice, the number of atoms per unit cell is $4$.

Number of atoms of A $= 4$

The number of octahedral voids is equal to the number of atoms in the lattice, which is $4$.

The number of tetrahedral voids is twice the number of atoms in the lattice, which is $8$.

Atoms of B occupy all octahedral voids and half of the tetrahedral voids.

Number of atoms of B $= 4 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 8 = 4 + 4 = 8$

The ratio of atoms of A to atoms of B is $4 : 8 = 1 : 2$.

The formula of the solid is $\text{AB}_2$.

Answer: $\text{AB}_2$

72176.subject: Physics
72176.text:
A very small circular loop of radius 'a' is initially (at $t = 0$) coplanar and concentric with a much larger fixed circular loop of radius 'b'. A constant current I flows in the larger loop. The smaller loop is rotated with a constant angular speed $\omega$ about the common diameter. The emf induced in the smaller loop as a function of time t is
(\mu_0$ = permeability of free space)$
72176.sol:
The magnetic field produced by the larger loop at its centre is given by

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2b}$

Since the smaller loop is very small (a \ll b$), the magnetic field over its area can be assumed to be uniform and equal to $B$.

The magnetic flux linked with the smaller loop at any time $t$ is

\Phi = \vec{B} \cdot \vec{A} = B A \cos(\omega t)$

Substituting $A = \pi a^2$ and $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2b}$, we get

$\Phi = \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2b}\right) (\pi a^2) \cos(\omega t)$

According to Faraday's law of induction, the induced emf is

$e = -\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt} = -\dfrac{d}{dt} \left[\left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I \pi a^2}{2b}\right) \cos(\omegat) \right]

$e = $\$left($\dfrac{\pi a^2 \mu_0 I}{2b}\right) \omega \sin$(\omegat)$

Answer: \$left($\dfrac{\pi a²\mu_0 I}{2b}\right)\omega\sin\omegat$

72335.subject: Physics
72335.text: If the maximum velocity in S.H.M. is 'V' then the average velocity during motion from one extreme to other extreme position will be
72335.sol:
Maximum velocity in S.H.M. is given by $V = A\omega$, where $A$ is the amplitude and $\omega$ is the angular frequency.

The displacement of the particle from one extreme position to the other extreme position is $2A$.

The time taken to travel from one extreme to the other is half of the time period, which is $t = \dfrac{T}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$.

Average velocity is the ratio of total displacement to the total time taken.

$v_{avg} = \dfrac{2A}{\dfrac{\pi}{\omega}} = \dfrac{2A\omega}{\pi}$

Substituting $V = A\omega$, we get:

$v_{avg} = \dfrac{2V}{\pi}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2V}{\pi}$

72547.text: Directions: The following items have four sentences, one of which is correct. Select the correct sentence.
options: No sooner than he reached the station the train left.
No sooner had he reached the station than the train left.
No sooner he had reached the station than the train left.
No sooner had he reached the station then the train left.
72547.sol:
The correct grammatical structure for sentences beginning with 'No sooner' is 'No sooner' followed by an inverted auxiliary verb and subject (e.g., 'had he' or 'did he'), and the two clauses must be joined by the conjunction 'than'.

Option (a) incorrectly places 'than' immediately after 'No sooner'.

Option (c) lacks the required inversion of the subject and auxiliary verb ('he had' instead of 'had he').

Option (d) incorrectly uses 'then' instead of 'than'.

Option (b) correctly follows the structure: 'No sooner had he reached the station than the train left.'

Answer: No sooner had he reached the station than the train left.

72581.subject: General Ability
72581.text:
In this section each item consists of six sentences that comprise a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The sequence of the middle four sentences has been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the answer sheet.

S1: National highways connect one state with another and are of national importance.
S6: These road systems are also known as primary road systems and are laid and operated under the supervision of the National Highway Authority of India.
P: They are important because whereas they constitute merely two per cent of the total road networks, they nevertheless carry 40 per cent of the total road traffic.
Q: The road infrastructure of the country is therefore crucial, and their construction and maintenance is of critical importance.
R: They bear the load of traffic because these roads connect long distances and pass through major cities and towns.
S: Since they cover the length and breadth of the nation and connect cities and towns, these highways are the primary facilitators of trade and connectivity.
72581.sol:
Sentence S1 introduces national highways and states that they are of "national importance".

Sentence P directly follows S1 by explaining the reason for this importance, starting with "They are important because..." and mentioning that they "carry 40 per cent of the total road traffic".

Sentence R logically follows P by explaining how they manage this traffic, starting with "They bear the load of traffic because..." and noting that they "pass through major cities and towns".

Sentence S builds upon the idea introduced in R. R mentions connecting long distances and cities, and S continues this thought with "Since they cover the length and breadth of the nation and connect cities and towns...".

Sentence Q serves as a concluding thought for the passage, summarizing that because of their role in trade and connectivity (mentioned in S), the road infrastructure is "therefore crucial, and their construction and maintenance is of critical importance".

Finally, S6 naturally follows Q, as "laid and operated" in S6 directly corresponds to "construction and maintenance" mentioned in Q.

Thus, the correct and most logical sequence is PRSQ.

Answer: PRSQ

73912.text: Which one among the following statements about arteries and veins in humans is NOT correct?

Arteries have thicker and more elastic walls compared to veins in general

76650.text:

The field of complex numbers cannot be ordered. Inequalities such as $z_1 > z_2$ or $z_1 < z_2$ are only defined if both $z_1$ and $z_2$ are purely real numbers.

76718.subject: Mathematics
76718.text:
Passage: Let $f(x)=\begin{cases} ax(x-1), & x< 1 \\ x-1, & 1\leq x\leq3 \\ px^2+qx+2, & x > 3 \end{cases}$
Given that $f(x)$ is continuous for all $x$ but not differentiable at $x=1$. Further $f'(x)$ is continuous at $x=3$.

Question: What is the value of $p$ ?
76718.sol:
For $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=3$, the left-hand limit and right-hand limit at $x=3$ must be equal.

$\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = 3 - 1 = 2$

$\lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = p(3)^2 + q(3) + 2 = 9p + 3q + 2$

Equating them, we get:

$9p + 3q + 2 = 2 \Rightarrow 9p + 3q = 0 \Rightarrow q = -3p$

The derivative of the function for $x \in (1, 3)$ is $f'(x) = 1$, and for $x > 3$ is $f'(x) = 2px + q$.

Since $f'(x)$ is continuous at $x=3$, the left-hand derivative and right-hand derivative at $x=3$ must be equal.

$\lim_{x \to 3^-} f'(x) = 1$

$\lim_{x \to 3^+} f'(x) = 2p(3) + q = 6p + q$

Equating them, we get:

$6p + q = 1$

Substituting $q = -3p$ into the above equation:

$6p - 3p = 1 \Rightarrow 3p = 1 \Rightarrow p = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3}$

77048.subject: Mathematics
77048.text:
Passage: Consider the differential equation $e^{x+y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{x-y}$.

Question: What is the solution of the differential equation with $y(0)=0$ ?
77048.sol:
The given differential equation is $e^{x+y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{x-y}$

$e^x e^y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^x e^{-y}$

$e^y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{-y}$

$e^{2y} dy = dx$

Integrating both sides:

$\int e^{2y} dy = \int dx$

$\dfrac{e^{2y}}{2} = x + C$

Given $y(0)=0$, substituting $x=0$ and $y=0$:

$\dfrac{e^0}{2} = 0 + C \Rightarrow C = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Substituting $C$ back into the equation:

$\dfrac{e^{2y}}{2} = x + \dfrac{1}{2}$

$e^{2y} = 2x + 1$

$2y = \ln(2x+1)$

80292.text: One set of the plant was grown at 12 hours day and 12 hours night period cycles and it flowered while in the other set night phase was interrupted by flash of light and it did not produce flower. Under which one of the following categories will you place this plant?
80292.sol:
Short day plants (SDP) require a relatively short-day light period (usually $8-10$ hours) and a continuous dark period of about 14-16 hours for subsequent flowering. If these plants are exposed to day lengths in excess of this critical point, they continue growing vegetatively and do not show flowering. Most of the winter flowering plants belong to this category. For example, Rice, coffee, soybean, tobacco, sugarcane, strawberry and chrysanthemum.
Related Theory
In long that plants, it was found that they can flower even under short day conditions, if a flash of light is provided to the plant during the long dark period. Thus, periods of darkness have inhibitory effect on flowering in these plants.

81269.subject: Chemistry
81269.text: The green paramagnetic species formed by heating KMnO$_4$ at $513$ K is
81269.sol:
When potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) is heated at $513\text{ K}$, it decomposes to form potassium manganate, manganese dioxide, and oxygen gas.

$2\text{KMnO}_4 \xrightarrow{513\text{ K}} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2$

The species $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$ (potassium manganate) is green in color.

In $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$, the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ is $+6$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{6+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^1$.

Since it contains one unpaired electron in the $d$-orbital, it is paramagnetic in nature.

Thus, the green paramagnetic species formed is $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$.

Answer: $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$

94519.text: A point source of heat of power $P$ is placed at the centre of a thin spherical shell of mean radius $R$. The material of the shell has thermal conductivity $K$. Calculate the thickness of the shell if the temperature difference between the outer and inner surfaces of the shell in steady-state is $T$.
94519.sol:
Consider a concentric spherical shell of radius $r$ and thickness $dr$ as shown in diagram. The radial rate of flow of heat through this shell in steady state will be,



$\text{H} = \dfrac{\text{d}\text{Q}}{\text{d}\text{t}} = - \text{KA}\dfrac{\text{d}\text{\theta}}{\text{d}\text{r}}$

[Negative sign is used because, with an increase in $r$, $\theta$ decreases.]

Now as for spherical shell $A = 4\pir^{2}$

So$\text{H} = - 4\text{\pi}r^{2}\text{K}\dfrac{\text{d}\text{\theta}}{\text{d}\text{r}}\text{or}{∫}_a^{b}\dfrac{\text{d}\text{r}}{\text{r}2} = - \dfrac{4\text{\pi}\text{K}}{H}{∫}_{\text{\theta}1}^{\text{\theta}2}\text{d}\text{\theta}$

which on integration and simplification gives

$\text{H} = \dfrac{\text{d}\text{Q}}{\text{d}\text{t}} = \text{K}4\text{\pi}ab\left({θ}_{1} - {θ}_{2}\right)\left(b - a\right)\text{...(i)}$

Now in steady state, as no heat is absorbed, the rate of loss of heat by conduction is equal to that of supply, i.e., $H = P$, and here

& ${θ}_{1} - {θ}_{2} = T$ and $\text{a} ≃ \text{b} = \text{R}$

So Equation (i) becomes,

& & $\text{P} = 4\piR^{2}\text{KT} \left(\text{b} - \text{a}\right)

i.e thickness of shell is \left(b - a\right) = \dfrac{4\piR^{2}\text{KT}}{P}$

95625.sol: The cell walls of archaebacteria are distinctive from those of eubacteria. Archaebacterial cell walls are composed of different polysaccharides and proteins, with no peptidoglycan. 100919.subject: Physics
100919.text: A block of mass $1 \text{ kg}$ is initially at rest on a rough horizontal surface having a coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu_k = 0.4$. It is pushed along the surface by a variable horizontal force. The applied force decreases linearly with position $x$ from $10 \text{ N}$ at $x = 0$ to $0 \text{ N}$ at $x = 10 \text{ m}$. The maximum kinetic energy attained by the block during its motion is: (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$)
100919.sol:
The kinetic friction acting on the block is $f_k = \mu_k mg = 0.4 \times 1 \times 10 = 4 \text{ N}$.

The applied force is $F(x) = 10 - x$.
The net force on the block is $F_{\text{net}} = F(x) - f_k = 10 - x - 4 = 6 - x$.

The kinetic energy of the block will be maximum when its acceleration becomes zero, which occurs when the net force is zero.
$F_{\text{net}} = 0 \Rightarrow 6 - x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 6 \text{ m}$.

The maximum kinetic energy is equal to the net work done on the block up to $x = 6 \text{ m}$.
$W_{\text{net}} = \int_{0}^{6} F_{\text{net}} \, dx = \int_{0}^{6} (6 - x) \, dx$
$W_{\text{net}} = \left[ 6x - \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{6} = \left( 36 - \dfrac{36}{2} \right) = 18 \text{ J}$.

Thus, the maximum kinetic energy attained is $18 \text{ J}$.

Answer: $18 \text{ J}$

102173.text:
Which statements are correct about degrees of freedom?

A. A molecule with $n$ degrees of freedom has ${n}^{2}$ different ways of storing energy.

B. Each degree of freedom is associated with $\dfrac{1}{2}RT$ average energy per mole.

C. A monoatomic gas molecule has $1$ rotational degree of freedom where as diatomic molecule has $2$ rotational degrees of freedom

D. ${CH}_{4}$ has a total to $6$ degrees of freedom.

Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
102173.sol:
According to the equipartition of energy, each degree of freedom carries $\dfrac{1}{2}RT$ energy per mole and total energy per mole of a gas having $n$ degrees of freedom is $\dfrac{1}{2}nRT$. Therefore, statement A is wrong and statement B is correct.

A monoatomic molecule only has translational degrees of freedom and does not have rotational degree of freedom. For a polyatomic model there are three rotational degrees of freedom and three translational degrees of freedom. Therefore, statement C is incorrect and statement D is correct.

102788.subject: Physics
102788.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : In a given situation of arrangement of charges, an additional charge is placed outside the Gaussian surface. In this situation, in the Gauss theorem \(\oint \overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}} \cdot \mathrm{d} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{s}}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\text{in }}}{\epsilon_0}, \mathrm{q}_{\text{in }}\) remains unchanged whereas electric field \(\vec{E}\) is changed.
Reason (R) : Electric field \(\vec{E}\) at any point on the Gaussian surface is due to inside charge only. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
102788.sol:
Assertion (A):
In a given situation of arrangement of charges, an additional charge is placed outside the Gaussian surface. In this situation, in the Gauss theorem \(\oint \mathrm{E} \cdot d \mathrm{s}=\frac{q_{\text{in }}}{\epsilon_0}, q_{\text{in }}\) remains unchanged whereas electric field \(\mathrm{E}\) is changed.
- This statement is true. According to Gauss's law, the total electric flux through a closed surface depends only on the charge enclosed within that surface. If an additional charge is placed outside the Gaussian surface, \(q_{\text{in }}\) does not change, but the electric field \(\mathrm{E}\) at points on the surface can change due to the influence of the external charge.
Reason (R):
Electric field \(\mathrm{E}\) at any point on the Gaussian surface is due to inside charge only.
- This statement is true as well. The electric field at any point on the Gaussian surface arises from the charges inside that surface. The external charge can affect the electric field, but for the purposes of applying Gauss's law, only the enclosed charges contribute to the electric flux.
Conclusion:
Both statements are true, and Reason (R) provides a correct explanation of Assertion (A). Answer: (1) Both (A) and \((\mathrm{R})\) are true and \((\mathrm{R})\) is the correct explanation of (A).

106988.subject: Chemistry
106988.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
106988.text:
The first four successive ionization enthalpies (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) for two unidentified Period 3 elements, X and Y, are given below:

Element X: 737, 1450, 7730, 10500
Element Y: 577, 1816, 2744, 11577

Identify the groups to which X and Y belong, and choose the correct relationship between their first ionization enthalpies ($\Delta_{i}H_{1}$).
options: X belongs to Group 2, Y belongs to Group 13, and $\Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{X}) < \Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{Y})$
X belongs to Group 2, Y belongs to Group 13, and $\Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{X}) > \Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{Y})$
X belongs to Group 1, Y belongs to Group 2, and $\Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{X}) < \Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{Y})$
X belongs to Group 13, Y belongs to Group 2, and $\Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{X}) > \Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{Y})$
106988.sol:
Analyze the successive ionization enthalpies to find the number of valence electrons:

For element X, there is a sudden large jump between the second ($1450 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) and third ($7730 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) ionization enthalpies. This indicates that X has 2 valence electrons, so it belongs to Group 2 (Magnesium).

For element Y, the large jump occurs between the third ($2744 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) and fourth ($11577 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) ionization enthalpies. This indicates that Y has 3 valence electrons, so it belongs to Group 13 (Aluminium).

Comparing their first ionization enthalpies: Element X (Mg) has a stable, fully filled 3s subshell ($3s^{2}$), whereas element Y (Al) has a $3s^{2} 3p^{1}$ configuration. The 3s electrons are more penetrating and tightly bound to the nucleus than the 3p electron. Therefore, it requires more energy to remove an electron from X than from Y.

Thus, X is in Group 2, Y is in Group 13, and $\Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{X}) > \Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{Y})$.

Answer: X belongs to Group 2, Y belongs to Group 13, and $\Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{X}) > \Delta_{i}H_{1}(\text{Y})$
